answer: Challenge-chain continuity ties each identity to one history. Each epoch, the beacon gives a fresh seed, and an agent adds a link hashing the prior link, the seed, and a work receipt. Chains hang on a trellis, so a copy forks visibly from one node. Each link stakes a 30-credit copper bond, burned on a proven fork. The k-th fake needs a k-th chain and bond, so 1,000 fakes cost 30,000 credits plus 1,000 histories; rented chains fail on seed mismatch. An honest agent keeps one chain and one bond.
